note: The first De Franceschi families this archive has been able to document in Carnia itself — the country the family says it came from, and where every account of its origin has until now been tradition rather than record.

mione.claim: In 1679 a list of village headmen recorded, at Mione: «Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo, Zuane d'Erman: questi tre nell'Istria, luogo imperiale» — a De Franceschi of Mione with a son, working in Istria, in the imperial place. Carlo De Franceschi, writing about 1873, said the family had come from Carnia and settled in Istria «intorno al 1700», and that De Franceschi were still living at Mione and Muina in his own day.
mione.found: They still were in 1939. Monsignor Lucio Soravito de Franceschi was born at Mione di Ovaro on 8 December 1939, ordained priest in 1963, professor of pastoral theology at the Udine seminary from 1977 and at the Faculty of Theology of Northern Italy from 1991, archpriest of Udine cathedral from 1999, and Bishop of Adria-Rovigo from 2004 to 2015. He died on 6 July 2019.
mione.why: Soravito is a Carnian house-name — soravìt, «above Vito's» — of the kind that fuses onto a surname to tell one branch of a village family from another. A Soravito de Franceschi at Mione is a De Franceschi of Mione with the house attached. Two hundred and sixty years after the headmen's list, the name is still in the village.

registers.what: The Archivio di Stato di Udine has digitised the Napoleonic civil registers of the Comune di Mione — fifty-nine volumes of births, marriages, deaths, marriage banns and marriage allegati, 1806 onward — and publishes them openly on the Antenati portal. Nobody had looked.
registers.index: The alphabetical index of births for 1806–1810 opens on three De Franceschi entries, the first three lines of the whole book: Anna-Maria, Anna-Cecilia and Gio: Batta. A few lines below are four Erman entries — the other family named in the 1679 headmen's list, still in the same village a hundred and thirty years later.

households.who: Osvaldo de Franceschi and Appolonia Salante
households.child: Anna Maria, born 30 December 1809 at eleven in the morning
households.note: Muina is the second village Carlo De Franceschi named in the 1870s when he said the family was still in Carnia.

households.who: Francesco de' Franceschi, aged about 26, and Margherita née Gortan
households.child: Anna Cecilia, born 14 January 1810 at three in the morning
households.note: He signs the register in his own hand. Gortan is one of the old surnames of the Canale di Gorto.

households.who: Osvaldo De Franceschi, aged 26, and Cattarina née Brencis
households.child: Giovanni Battista, born 15 October 1810 at ten in the morning
households.note: He signs too. Whether he is the same man as the Osvaldo of Muina ten months earlier is not clear: the wives differ, the villages differ and the trades differ, so the archive treats them as two households and says so.

households.who: Pasqua de' Franceschi, wife of Pietro Luchin
households.child: named as the mother in act 2 of 1810
households.note: A De Franceschi daughter married into the Luchin of Mione.

registers.read: Three things follow. First, the family is simply there, in the village, in the ordinary registers — not merely listed as working abroad. Second, one of them is a TAILOR, which is exactly the trade of the cramars who walked the road of the Furlans into Istria from the sixteenth century; another is a carpenter and the rest are farmers, which is the ordinary spread of a mountain commune. And third, the name they gave a son born at Mione on 15 October 1810 was GIOVANNI BATTISTA — the name of the man Carlo De Franceschi said built the family's house at Gologorica in 1711, and the name of the farmer of house 5 at Gračišće born in 1787.

paluzza.what: The earliest of them. Zuanne is the Venetian form of Giovanni — the same name the 1679 list gives the man of Mione.

paluzza.with: Maria Silverio, daughter of Gasparo Silverio and Orsola Moser

paluzza.what: Daughter of Daniele and Maria Silverio.
Their sons Francesco, born 14 December 1807 at Naunina in Paluzza, and Pietro Antonio, born 5 June 1810.
Their son Pietro, born 1851 at Paluzza, married Maria Lazzaro — and dead at forty-four in the civic hospital at San Daniele del Friuli on 30 March 1895, entered in the register as a mason.
Their daughter Maria, born 1865 at Paluzza.
Married out; their son Giovanni Daniele born at Paluzza in 1810.
Married out; their daughter Maria Maddalena born at Paluzza in 1810.
Married out; their son Giuseppe born at Tolmezzo in 1817.

ovaro.what: Their son Egidio, at Ovaro. Gortani is one of the old surnames of the Canale di Gorto.
Named with an Antonio, an Angelica, a Carlo and a Pasqualina.

muina.heading: The house at Muina, four generations deep
muina.intro: The marriage register goes further than the births. Napoleonic marriage acts read the couple's birth certificates into the record, and birth certificates name the grandparents. One act at Mione therefore reaches further back into Carnia than anything else this project has found.

chain.what: Dead before 1808. Named only as «qm. Leonardo» — the late Leonardo — in his son's style. If his grandson was born in 1788 and his son was of age to marry by about 1785, Leonardo belongs to a generation born somewhere between about 1710 and 1740.

chain.who: Antonio de Franceschi, son of the late Leonardo, and Maria née Corva
chain.what: Farmers of Muina. Both alive in 1808: Antonio gave his written consent to his son's marriage on 25 October 1807, three months before the wedding.

chain.who: Osvaldo de Franceschi and Appolonia Salante
chain.what: He was born at Muina on 14 March 1788 and was twenty when he married on 28 January 1808; a farmer, and he signs his own name. She was born at Muina on 3 May 1782, daughter of Antonio, son of the late Pietro Salante, and Speranza née Micoli.
Born at Muina at eleven in the morning on 30 December 1809, and presented to the registrar by the midwife Speranza Salante — who was, by the marriage act, her own maternal grandmother.

muina.leonardo: One name in that chain is worth stopping on. Carlo De Franceschi, writing to Kobler about 1873, said the house at Gologorica was built in 1711 by his trisavolo «Giambattista del fu Leonardo» — Giovanni Battista, son of the late Leonardo. And here, in the Carnian village Carlo said the family came from, is an «Antonio qm. Leonardo de Franceschi». The generations do not line up for the two Leonardos to be the same man: Carlo's Leonardo was the father of someone building a house in 1711, while this one is the grandfather of a boy born in 1788, three generations later. What it shows is that Leonardo was a name this family used, in this village — and that is the first time any name from Carlo's account of his own ancestry has turned up in a Carnian De Franceschi household in a register.
muina.witnesses: The four witnesses were Angelo Micoli, fifty-seven; Floriano Micoli, forty; Giuseppe Varnier, forty-eight; and Odorico Micoli, twenty-three — all farmers of Muina. The registrar was Valentino Lupieri. Micoli, Lupieri, Gortan, Brencis, Salante, Corva, Varnier: the same dozen surnames run through every document in this village.

households1806.heading: Five De Franceschi households at Mione and Muina, 1806–1810
households1806.intro: Put every act together and the village stops being a name in a tradition and becomes a set of families with trades, wives, in-laws and children. All of it inside five years of one small commune's registers.

rows.who: Osvaldo de Franceschi († before 1806) and Catterina née Fabris
rows.evidence: Named in their daughter's marriage act of 7 August 1806. Giacoma, born 25 May 1789, seventeen years two months and twelve days old, married Ignazio di Prato, a merchant of Chialina. She signs herself «Giacoma de Franceschi q.m Osualdo». Her father had given written consent on 7 September 1805, so he died between then and the wedding.

rows.who: Antonio de Franceschi, son of the late Leonardo, and Maria née Corva
rows.evidence: Named in their son's marriage act of 28 January 1808, with Antonio's written consent of 25 October 1807. Leonardo, Antonio's father, was already dead.

rows.who: Osvaldo de Franceschi (b. 14 March 1788) and Appolonia Salante (b. 3 May 1782)
rows.evidence: Married 28 January 1808. Daughter Anna Maria born 30 December 1809, presented by the midwife Speranza Salante — Appolonia's own mother.

rows.who: Osvaldo de Franceschi and Valentina, or Cattarina, née Prencis
rows.evidence: Married 6 August 1807 (marriage index). Son Giovanni Battista born 15 October 1810, where the mother is written Cattarina nata Brencis — probably the same woman under a second baptismal name.

rows.who: Francesco de' Franceschi (b. about 1784) and Margherita née Gortan
rows.evidence: Daughter Anna Cecilia born 14 January 1810. He signs the register himself.

rows.who: Pasqua de' Franceschi, wife of Pietro Luchin
rows.evidence: Named as the mother in act 2 of 1810.

households1806.tailors: Look at who witnessed Giacoma's wedding in 1806: Gio: Battà Prencis, thirty-six, tailor; Gio: Battà del Missier, fifty-four, tailor; Giuseppe Pol, thirty-four, tailor; Pietro Rupil of Ovasta, thirty-six, tailor. Four tailors standing up at a merchant's wedding in an alpine village of a few hundred people. That is the cramar economy in a single line — the needle trades of the Canale di Gorto that sent men down the road of the Furlans into Istria every autumn from the sixteenth century. Francesco de' Franceschi of Mione was one of them in 1810.
households1806.micoli: And the registrar in 1806 is Giovanni Micoli-Toscano, with Battà Micoli-Toscano as secretary. The Micoli Toscano family archive at Mione is already on this project's research log as the place that holds the Gorto contracts naming the Erman who travelled to Istria with Zuane De Franceschi in 1679. In 1806 they are running the commune.

deaths.heading: And eight deaths in the same five years
deaths.intro: The register of the dead for the Comune di Mione, 1806–1810, carries eight De Franceschi entries. Read with the births, they turn a set of names into a family that was living and dying in one village.

rows.name: Leonarda Defranceschi
rows.note: Leonarda is the feminine of Leonardo — the name that stands at the head of the Muina chain.

rows.name: Anna Cecilia Defranceschi
rows.note: Born 14 January 1810 to Francesco the tailor and Margherita Gortan. She lived eleven days.

rows.name: Sebastiano Defranceschi, chierico
rows.note: A cleric — chierico, a man in minor orders. The only one of the name in these registers.

deaths.read: Two of these change what was already written on this page. Anna Cecilia, whose birth act was quoted above as evidence that a De Franceschi tailor lived at Mione in 1810, died eleven days after she was born; her father had carried her to the town hall at three in the morning and was back within a fortnight. And there is a Leonarda in 1808 and a Sebastiano in minor orders in 1810 — a family big enough to put a son into the church and to keep reusing its own names. The same index also records Corva and Erman deaths: Osvaldo Corva of Agrons in 1807, Teresa Corva of Muina the same year, and three Erman.

deepest.heading: The allegati, and the deepest name of all
deepest.intro: Napoleonic marriage files carry allegati — the supporting papers. Giacoma's file at Mione holds two, and one of them is a parish certificate written out by hand, sealed, and stamped with a two-and-sixpence revenue stamp of the Kingdom of Italy.
deepest.quote: Certifico io sottoscritto Parroco della Pieve Matrice di Gorto a parte Luvincis, come Giacoma figlia legitima e naturale di Osualdo quondam Gio: Batta de' Franceschi di Mione, e di Cattarina sua moglie, essa è nata li 25 del mese di Maggio nell'anno 1789, come consta dal Libro dei Battezzi.
deepest.trans: I, the undersigned parish priest of the mother church of Gorto at Luincis, certify that Giacoma, lawful and natural daughter of Osvaldo, son of the late GIOVANNI BATTISTA de' Franceschi of Mione, and of Cattarina his wife, was born on the 25th of May in the year 1789, as appears from the Book of Baptisms.
deepest.why: That pushes the Mione family back one more generation, to a GIOVANNI BATTISTA DE' FRANCESCHI who was already dead by 1789. And it means that both of the names Carlo De Franceschi gave for his own ancestors — Giambattista, and the Leonardo who was Giambattista's father — occur in the eighteenth-century De Franceschi of Mione: a Giovanni Battista dead before 1789, and an Antonio son of the late Leonardo. Carlo said the family came from Carnia. In the village he named, the two names he used are the two names in the register.
deepest.care: This is still not a descent. Giovanni Battista and Leonardo were among the commonest names in Friuli, the generations do not align, and no document yet connects any Mione household to any Istrian one. What has changed is that the claim now has a place, a parish, a set of households and two matching names — instead of a single line in a list of headmen.
deepest.next: The certificate also names the record that would settle it: the LIBRO DEI BATTEZZI of the Pieve Matrice di Gorto at Luincis, which in 1806 still held baptisms back beyond 1789. That book, and the parish's marriage and death books, are the next thing to ask for — from the parish itself or from the Archivio Storico Diocesano at Udine. Ask for De Franceschi at Mione and Muina between 1650 and 1800.
